S1_REFEREE:
**Take-aways from S1 (SIMULATED, 200 runs per cell):**
- **Rank-deficient plug-ins return F̂ = 0 and D_BS = +∞ until the floor is resolved.** For linear inversion + CPTP projection on the δ = 2√p pair, the median F̂ is 0.13 / 0.444 / 0.68 / 0.708 at p = 1e-2 and N = 1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5 / 1e6 (truth 0.711). It is still 0.433 at p = 1e-3, N = 1e6, and 5.88e-16 at p = 1e-4, N = 1e5. Plug-in D_BS is +∞ in 85% of runs at p = 1e-3, N = 1e6. The rank-1 and rank-2 fits give F̂ = 0 at every N.
- **Plug-in errors are mostly on the loose side, but not always.** At p = 1e-2, N = 1e6 the overclaim fraction of F̂ is 0.18 (LI) and 0.21 (MLE). The hedged MLE (β = 1/2) overclaims in 96% of runs at p = 1e-4, N = 1e2 (median 0.888 against a truth of 0.707). No plug-in estimator is therefore a certified converse.
- **E₁ and F_U plug-ins do not need the floor.** At N = 1e4 the median LI E₁ is 0.101 at p = 1e-2 (truth 0.0988) and 0.0335 at p = 1e-3 (truth 0.0316).
- **The S1 grid stops at N = 1e6 for every p.** The p = 1e-4, N = 1e6 cell was completed in this session. The N = 1e7–1e9 cells of the original plan were not run.
S2_COVTEXT:
**Reading the coverage table (SIMULATED).**
- Plug-in F̂ used directly as a converse is valid (F̂_plug ≤ truth) in 0.782 (p = 0.01, N = 1e+06), 0.918 (p = 0.001, N = 1e+08), 0.681 (p = 0.001, N = 1e+10), 0.994 (p = 0.0001, N = 1e+10) of runs. It is not a certified bound at any of these points.
- The Weyl floor LCB has a negative median at every coverage point (-0.0187 at p = 0.01, N = 1e+06), (-0.00187 at p = 0.001, N = 1e+08), (2.63e-4 at p = 0.001, N = 1e+10), (-1.87e-4 at p = 0.0001, N = 1e+10), so the floor itself is not yet certified at the N where the box certificates are within a factor 2. This is the p⁻² of the operator-norm route.
S2_TEXT:
**Summary of S2 (opposite side; FITTED exponents of N_req ∝ p^−a):**
- On the δ = 2√p pair the Hoeffding-box bounds cost p^−1.93 (F̂) and p^−1.94 (D_BS). The plug-in F̂ reaches 10% accuracy at p^−2.04, and the Weyl-certified floor at p^−2.00 (analytic).
- On the same pair E₁ costs p^−0.99 and F_U p^−1.26. These are factor-2 criteria, and the true values shrink (E₁ ∝ √p, −ln F_U ∝ p), so this is not a floor effect.
- On the δ = 1 rad pair, E₁ and F_U are within a factor 2 at the first grid point (10³ shots per setting) for every p, while F̂ costs p^−0.90.
- The v5 theorem route (Cor 10.7/10.8) is vacuous on the whole grid up to N = 10¹².
S3_TEXT: **Summary of S3 (SIMULATED, plug-in only).** For the CNOT with local depolarising noise, λ_min J = p²/4, the square of the qubit floor up to constants. The N at which 90% of plug-in runs are within 10% therefore scales as λ_min⁻² ∝ p⁻⁴ (table above, one-decade grid). This matches the n-qubit form λ̃ = (p/4)ⁿ that enters N1–N4. A certified CNOT pipeline was not built.
HEADLINE: **Headline.** Near the noisy Hadamard N_p = D_p∘H, the geometric-fidelity and Belavkin–Staszewski converses can be certified from finite data, at a cost set by the Choi floor λ̃ = p/4. Certifying −ln F̂ to η = 0.05 through a diamond-norm ball (Pauli tomography + Theorem C) takes 3.6e11–3.6e15 channel uses per channel for p = 1e-2…1e-4, with fitted slope −2.000. Direct Pauli-error estimation in the known frame takes 1.2e6–1.2e8, with slope −1.00 [95% CI −1.05, −0.96] (FITTED). So the ball is wasteful by a factor ≈ 750/λ̃ (ratio × λ̃ = 690–780), as Theorem C and N1–N4 predict. Every converse-side certificate covered the truth in 1000/1000 runs at every p (target ≥ 0.95; SIMULATED). The D_BS upper bound scales like F̂ (slope −1.00). Hockey-stick and Uhlmann certificates through the same ball cost the same at every p (slopes 0.000, −0.008). Correction: the earlier S2/S2b SDP bounds (max F̂, min D over the region) lie on the opposite side and do not certify the converses (§0).
S2b_TEXT:
**Discussion of S2b.**
- **Slopes (FITTED).** The diamond-ball certificate costs N ∝ p^−2.000 and direct Pauli-error estimation N ∝ p^−1.00. The D_BS upper bound from (b) costs N ∝ p^−1.00. These are exactly the Θ(1/(ηλ̃)²) and Θ(1/(η²λ̃)) laws. The ratio (a)/(b) times λ̃ stays within 690–780 across p, so the waste of the ball is a factor ≈ 7e2/λ̃. Part of that constant comes from the 6× larger number of settings in (a), and part from the variance-blind 36t trace-norm radius.
- **Constants against N2–N4.** (b) sits 290–330× above the N3 scale c₀/(η²λ̃), and at 0.65–0.73× the N4 sufficient budget, which is for Bell-basis measurement at δ_f = 0.05. (a) sits 1.5e6× above the incoherent-learner bound N2 evaluated at the sharp radius ε = 4ηλ̃. That gap is the constant of a non-optimal learner, not a different scaling. The requirement κ = ε_tr/(2λ_min) ≤ η, with λ_min = p/2, ε_tr = 36t and t = √(ln(1440)/(2N_set)), alone gives N = 18·36²·ln(1440)/(2η²p²) ≈ 3.4e7/p² channel uses (observed: 3.6e7/p² at p = 1e-2). N2 at the sharp radius is ≈ 24/p². Two caveats apply to N3 here. It is proved for the estimand F̂(Ad_{PU}, Ψ), a unitary against a Pauli channel, with success probability 2/3. Our estimand is F̂ between two noisy channels, and the criterion is the median run. The plotted line is therefore the proved scale of the intrinsic cost, not a rigorous bound for this pair. It lies below every measured point.
- **η-dependence (FITTED over η ∈ {0.1, 0.05, 0.025}).** (a): N ∝ η^−b with b = 1.94. Since κ is linear in the radius, the asymptotic value is 2. (b): b = 1.65–1.76. This is pre-asymptotic: ln F̂ responds sub-linearly to relative changes of the floor rates at these widths. It is consistent with the N4 upper bound ∝ η^−2.
- **Contrast.** Through the same diamond ball, E₁ and F_U are certified at p-independent cost: slope 0.000 [−0.003, +0.002] and −0.008 [−0.017, +0.001]. At p = 1e-4 the E₁ certificate needs 3.5e7 channel uses, against 3.6e15 for F̂ through the same ball. The F_U route uses the purified-distance triangle inequality, which costs ∝ η^−4 but contains no λ̃.
- **Coverage (SIMULATED).** At every p and for both pipelines, the F̂ lower bound covered the truth in 1000 of 1000 runs. The D_BS upper bound of (b) covered it in 1000 of 1000. The lowest 95% Clopper–Pearson limit on a coverage of 1000/1000 is 0.9963. The regions are conservative (union bound), as expected.
- **Opposite side (§3.5).** The SDP bounds give the same picture: (a) trace-norm ball −2.00, (a′) Hoeffding box −1.96, (a″) Clopper–Pearson box −1.02, (b) Pauli polytope −0.99. The model-free Clopper–Pearson box in probability space reaches slope ≈ −1 on that side. On the converse side the exact LCB over that box is a concave minimisation over an 18-dimensional polytope ∩ CPTP, which was not attempted. Whether model-free tomography attains the 1/λ̃ law for the converse is therefore not settled by these runs.
- **Model assumption.** (b) is valid only if both channels are Pauli channels in the known frames U₁ and U₀. Any coherent error outside the model invalidates it. (a) assumes nothing beyond the tomography model.
